newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest power again holds mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest power again holds mostly steady.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were again mostly steady Thursday with primarily near and above normal temperatures moderating power demand, industry sources said.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Friday peak, non-firm power prices were pegged steady at $16.50-18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), brokers and marketers said.
MAPP temperatures were expected to be near normal under cloud into Saturday then turn slightly milder on Sunday and Monday with averages of two to four degrees above normal.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP next day power was said to be unchanged at $11.00-13.00.

In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Friday were assessed slightly higher at $17.00-18.00 from $16.50-17.50 on Wednesday for Thursday delivery, the sources said.
Temperatures in MAIN were expected to be near to slightly below normal with cloudiness into Saturday, then turn milder with temperatures two to four degrees above normal Sunday and Monday.
MAIN off peak next day power was said to be steady at $11.00-13.00 per MWh.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Friday were said to be discussed slightly lower at 15.50-16.50 from $16.00-18.00 on Wednesday, the sources said.
Temperatures in ECAR were expected to be above normal through Saturday, then turning milder Sunday and Monday with temperatures averaging five to 10 degrees above normal.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm next day delivery were notionally assessed steady at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.
March ECAR was said to be talked steady to lower at $20.10-20.50 from $20.20-20.75 per MWh on Wednesday.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Friday delivery were pegged lower at $17.00-19.00 in the north from $19.00-21.00 on Wednesday, while in the south next day peak power was assessed at $17.00-18.00 from $17.00-19.00 per MWh.
Off-peak non-firm next day prices throughout SPP were assessed steady at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.
In SPP, temperatures were forecast to average five to 10 degrees below normal through the weekend with snow in the north and rain in the south.
March peak SPP was talked at $19.80-20.20 from $19.95-20.30 on Wednesday, the sources said.
